Set $y = \frac{2}{x^2 - 1}$ and solve for $x$ on the domain $x < -1$ (where $x$ is negative):
$$x^2 - 1 = \frac{2}{y} \implies x^2 = \frac{2}{y} + 1$$
$$x = -\sqrt{\frac{2}{y} + 1} \quad (\text{taking the negative root since } x < -1)$$

Write the inverse function in terms of $x$:
$$f^{-1}(x) = -\sqrt{\frac{2}{x} + 1}$$

Take the square root (since $x < -1 \implies x^2 - 1 > 0$, the inner fraction must be positive):
$$\frac{2}{x^2 - 1} = 2 \implies x^2 - 1 = 1 \implies x^2 = 2$$

Select the root satisfying the domain $x < -1$:
$$x = -\sqrt{2} \quad (\approx -1.41)$$
